name: OpenAI Build Week
theme: Global online hackathon to build working projects with Codex and GPT-5.6 across consumer, work/productivity, developer tooling, and education tracks.
team_size: No limit on team size per FAQ; entrants may submit as individuals, teams, or organizations. Some prizes have team-size-related prize delivery limits, including up to two DevDay/Exchange passes for first-place teams.
required_or_encouraged_tech: Codex required and must be demonstrated in the submission
GPT-5.6 required, but it does not need to be used for the whole project
/feedback Codex Session ID from the primary build thread required
Public YouTube demo video under 3 minutes with audio explaining what was built and how Codex and GPT-5.6 were used
Code repository required, public with relevant licensing or private shared with testing@devpost.com and build-week-event@openai.com
README with setup instructions, sample data if needed, running/testing guidance, and explanation of Codex/GPT-5.6 contribution
For plugins or developer tools: installation instructions, supported platforms, and a demo instance, sandbox, test account, or other judge testing path
Open source libraries, frameworks, third-party SDKs/APIs/data allowed only with proper authorization and license compliance
Devpost Hackathons Plugin is optional, not required to enter or win
prizes: 1st Place | Apps for Your Life: $15,000 cash, up to two DevDay/Exchange passes, OpenAI Developers promotion, Codex Team meeting, 1-year Pro Account
2nd Place | Apps for Your Life: $10,000 cash, OpenAI Developers promotion, 1-year Pro Account
1st Place | Work & Productivity: $15,000 cash, up to two DevDay/Exchange passes, OpenAI Developers promotion, Codex Team meeting, 1-year Pro Account
2nd Place | Work & Productivity: $10,000 cash, OpenAI Developers promotion, 1-year Pro Account
1st Place | Developer Tools: $15,000 cash, up to two DevDay/Exchange passes, OpenAI Developers promotion, Codex Team meeting, 1-year Pro Account
2nd Place | Developer Tools: $10,000 cash, OpenAI Developers promotion, 1-year Pro Account
1st Place | Education: $15,000 cash, up to two DevDay/Exchange passes, OpenAI Developers promotion, Codex Team meeting, 1-year Pro Account
2nd Place | Education: $10,000 cash, OpenAI Developers promotion, 1-year Pro Account

facts.claim: The submission deadline is July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM Pacific Time.

The schedule page lists submissions from July 13, 2026 at 9:00 AM PDT to July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM PDT, judging from July 22, 2026 at 9:00 AM PDT to August 09, 2026 at 5:00 PM PDT, and winners announced August 12, 2026 at 2:00 PM PDT.

The official rules list registration from July 9, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT to July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM PT, submission from July 13, 2026 at 9:00 AM PT to July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM PT, judging from July 22, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT to August 5, 2026 at 5:00 PM PT, and winners announced on or around August 12, 2026 at 2:00 PM PT.
The hackathon is online, public, managed by Devpost, sponsored by OpenAI, and tagged Machine Learning/AI, DevOps, and Productivity.

Eligible participants must be at least the age of majority in their residence and in supported countries/territories that support OpenAI API services, subject to exclusions including jurisdictions where U.S. or local law prohibits participation or prize receipt.
facts.source: https://openai.devpost.com/rules lines 118-128 and untrusted evidence rules eligibility text

facts.claim: Projects must be built with Codex and GPT-5.6 and fit one of four tracks: Apps for Your Life, Work and Productivity, Developer Tools, or Education.
Projects must install and run consistently on their intended platform and function as depicted in the video or text description.
facts.source: https://openai.devpost.com/rules Project Requirements text in supplied evidence; https://openai.devpost.com/rules lines 182-204 for submission requirements

facts.claim: Pre-existing projects are allowed only if meaningfully extended during the submission period, with documentation distinguishing prior work from new work and evidence such as timestamped Codex session logs or dated commit history.

Submissions require a working project, category, text description, under-3-minute public YouTube demo with audio covering what was built and how Codex and GPT-5.6 were used, repository URL, README, and /feedback Codex Session ID.
Judges may test projects but are not required to; they may use the demo link, sandbox, or test account provided.
No changes can be made to submissions after the Submission Period ends on July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM PT.
Stage One judging is pass/fail for baseline viability, theme fit, and reasonable application of required APIs/SDKs featured in the hackathon.
Stage Two uses four equally weighted criteria: Technological Implementation, Design, Potential Impact, and Quality of the Idea.
Tie-breaking follows the listed criterion order, starting with Technological Implementation, then subsequent listed criteria as needed.
The project gallery was not published at time of access, so previous or current finalist/winner analysis from the gallery was unavailable.
The Resources page states all available $100 Codex credits had been given out, while the event still welcomes free-tier participation.

The official GPT-5.6 docs describe Programmatic Tool Calling, multi-agent beta, explicit prompt caching, persisted reasoning, max reasoning effort, pro mode, token efficiency, frontend design improvements, intent understanding, and original image detail handling.
The GPT-5.6 docs recommend the Responses API for reasoning, tool-calling, and multi-turn workflows and describe model choices gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, and gpt-5.6-luna.
Codex can be used from ChatGPT desktop, ChatGPT web, Codex CLI, Codex IDE extension, and Codex cloud according to the ChatGPT Learn quickstart navigation and setup content.

inference.claim: Technical Implementation is strategically decisive despite equal weights because it is both an equal Stage Two criterion and the first tie-break criterion.
inference.rationale: Rules say Stage Two criteria are equally weighted, but tie-breaking starts with the first listed criterion, Technological Implementation.

inference.claim: Runnable, judge-friendly demos are strategically important because judges may not build the project from scratch and are not required to test it.
inference.rationale: FAQ says judges may test but are not required to and will use provided demo/sandbox/test account if they do.

inference.claim: Projects that merely wrap GPT-5.6 or mention Codex decoratively are weak fits.
inference.rationale: Rules and FAQ require meaningful Codex and GPT-5.6 use, demo narration, README explanation, and /feedback evidence.

inference.claim: The strongest sponsor alignment is likely demonstrable Codex-accelerated engineering plus GPT-5.6 capabilities such as tool-heavy workflows, multi-agent coordination, reasoning, prompt caching, or polished frontend/product experience.
inference.rationale: Judging emphasizes Codex use, non-trivial implementation, coherent product experience, impact, and novelty; OpenAI docs highlight these GPT-5.6/Codex capabilities.

inference.claim: Education may have an expert strategic lens because the judge list includes OpenAI VP of Education Leah Belsky.
inference.rationale: The overview page lists judge roles, including a VP of Education, but no per-track judging assignments are published.

inference.claim: High participant count implies heavy collision pressure around broad AI assistant archetypes and template-like productivity/education apps.
inference.rationale: The overview and tabs show roughly 42,000 participants, and the tracks map directly onto common AI hackathon archetypes.

judging_criteria.name: Stage One: baseline viability
judging_criteria.notes: Project must reasonably fit the theme and reasonably apply required APIs/SDKs featured in the hackathon.

judging_criteria.name: Technological Implementation
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: Equal Stage Two weight; first tie-break priority
judging_criteria.notes: Assesses thorough and skillful Codex use, genuine effort, and working non-trivial implementation.

judging_criteria.name: Design
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: Equal Stage Two weight; second tie-break priority
judging_criteria.notes: Assesses whether the project is working/runnable and has a complete, coherent product experience rather than just a proof of concept.

judging_criteria.name: Potential Impact
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: Equal Stage Two weight; third tie-break priority
judging_criteria.notes: Assesses credible, specific real-problem framing for a real audience and whether the demonstrated solution addresses it.

judging_criteria.name: Quality of the Idea
judging_criteria.weight_or_priority: Equal Stage Two weight; fourth tie-break priority
judging_criteria.notes: Assesses creativity, novelty, and differentiation from existing concepts.

sanitized_brief: OpenAI Build Week is an online public hackathon sponsored by OpenAI and administered by Devpost with submissions due July 21, 2026 at 5:00 PM PDT. Build a working project using Codex and GPT-5.6 in exactly one track: Apps for Your Life, Work and Productivity, Developer Tools, or Education. Required submission materials include a text description, public YouTube demo under 3 minutes with audio explaining what was built and how Codex and GPT-5.6 were used, a testable code repository, README with setup/sample-data guidance and Codex/GPT-5.6 contribution notes, and a /feedback Codex Session ID. Stage One is pass/fail for viability/theme/tool fit; Stage Two criteria are equally weighted: Technological Implementation, Design, Potential Impact, and Quality of the Idea, with ties resolved in that listed order. Strategically important sponsor capabilities include Codex build workflows, GPT-5.6 reasoning/tool-calling/multi-agent/prompt-caching/persisted-reasoning/frontend strengths, and judge-friendly runnable demos or sandboxes. Blacklist labels: generic tutor/flashcard, wellness chatbot, resume optimiser, PDF summariser, meeting-notes bot, generic support/workflow chatbot, generic DevOps/log assistant, dashboard-only analytics, recommendation-only lists, generic sponsor API wrapper, and unauthorized-data projects.
